chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the voluntary fasting one whose need presents itself to him. He (peace be upon him) said: He has the choice between himself and Asr; and if he remains until Asr, then it becomes clear to him that he should fast, if he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ الْمُتَطَوِّعِ: The voluntary faster (one fasting nafl, not obligatory)
key_terms.الْحَاجَةُ: Need (referring to eating, drinking, or other things that break the fast)
key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: Asr (the afternoon prayer, serving as the cutoff time for establishing voluntary fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking a voluntary fast before Asr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the juristic status of voluntary fasting (sawm al-tatawwu') by establishing the Asr prayer as the critical threshold for intention (niyyah). It clarifies that while breaking the fast is permissible before Asr, remaining until Asr without eating solidifies the fast, allowing completion even if the specific intention was formed later, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of voluntary acts compared to obligatory ones.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Husayn Bin Usman, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the voluntary Fasts, a need presents itself to him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is with the choice what is between him and Al-Asr; and if he were to remain until Al-Asr, then he changes his mind, for him would be that he Fasts. So, if he does not happen to have that intention, so for him is that he Fasts that day, if he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al- Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who fasts an optional fast but he faces a certain issue of his needs. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has the choice until al-‘Asr (later afternoon). If he waits until al-‘Asr and then it occurs to him to fast, if he did not have the intention for fasting, he can fast that day by the will of Allah.’”
